## TRA Timeline

#### De-SPAC business combination and TRA execution

- 2019-01-22: 8-K announces the merger agreement and files form-of TRA as exhibit 10.2
- 2019-07-11: Thunder Bridge Acquisition domesticates from Cayman to Delaware and merges with Hawk Parent Holdings LLC, forming Up-C; TRA executed between Repay Holdings Corporation and the Repay Unitholders (pre-business-combination members of Hawk Parent), paying 100% of the Net Tax Benefit from Section 754 basis step-ups on exchanges plus Imputed Interest
- 2019-07-11: 8-K files the executed TRA as exhibit 10.2

#### Payments in force

- 2026-Q1: $13.7M of TRA payments disclosed in the Q1 2026 10-Q cash flow statement (vs. $16.3M in Q1 2025); contract paying out normally, no termination event recorded

## Explanation

Repay Holdings' July 11, 2019 de-SPAC business combination (Thunder Bridge Acquisition merging into Hawk Parent Holdings LLC) created a TRA paying 100% of the Net Tax Benefit (not the typical 85%) to the Repay Unitholders, covering Section 754 basis adjustments on exchanges of Post-Merger Repay Units for Class A common stock plus Imputed Interest on payments. No amendments, terminations, or waivers have been filed. The contract pays out routinely; the 2025 10-K and Q1 2026 10-Q confirm continuing fair-value carrying and $13.7M of Q1 2026 cash payments. Repay announced a Strategic Review Process on March 3, 2025 and adopted a Stockholder Rights Agreement at a 12.5% threshold on April 13, 2026; if a sale closes, the Change-of-Control acceleration in Section 3.1(b) and Section 4.1 would be the relevant trigger to monitor. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record, the same-contract reasoning across the three TRA versions, and the 95%/5% wire-routing detail.
